criteria.note: In-session resume is the wired default. bin/warp cmd_fleet builds fleet.InSessionWaiter when no waiter is injected; the selftest drives cmd_fleet with waiter=None over a spy and asserts exactly one in-session default waiter is built, it waits until the governor resume epoch (4242) then re-checks the desired count, and a backed-off pool that then drains spawns nothing (start called zero times). Over an injected clock, so the gate never sleeps. The default path creates no timer and no background process.

The external supervisor is opt-in and off by default. Importing supervisor.py and not calling install() leaves no timer and no service unit (selftest over a temp unit dir). Nothing reaches install/status/uninstall except the explicit warp supervisor subcommand; warp supervisor with no action and install with no schedule both fail loud (nonzero) touching no systemd. With no explicit install the fleet behaves exactly as the AC1 in-session default.

Right architecture, visible, removable. install() generates a standard systemd user timer plus a oneshot service ([Timer] OnCalendar + WantedBy=timers.target, [Service] Type=oneshot + ExecStart), computes OnCalendar from the governor resume epoch, enables through an injected runner plus daemon-reload, and is idempotent and confined (re-run writes byte-identical units, exactly two files in the injected dir). status reports installed/is-enabled/is-active through the runner; uninstall disables and removes both units cleanly and is idempotent. All over a temp XDG dir and a fake systemctl; the real user systemd is never touched. It is a user timer, not a system crontab, resident daemon, lock-refresher, or headless polling loop.

The session-launch primitive is a fail-loud reference seam. launch_session raises SupervisorLaunchError unwired and delegates to an injected launcher when wired. install runs only systemctl subcommands (daemon-reload/enable/disable/is-enabled/is-active) and never launches a session; a fabricate-a-schedule install is refused (RULE #6); and a launch spy proves install never calls launch_session by default or as a side effect. supervisor.py imports no subprocess at module top and never calls os.fork or os.system; RealSystemctl lazily imports subprocess only to run systemctl. No detached process is created by default, by the gate, or by the in-session path.

.warp/supervisor.py ships in the canonical engine and all seven packs byte-identical (content and mode), and the bin/warp supervisor subcommand ships identically (100755). The three new capability entries are honest and correctly not repo-only because they ship (fleet_in_session_resume_default and fleet_external_supervisor mechanical, fleet_supervisor_session_launch reference); all homes resolve in the shipped engine under the WARP-0906 honesty check (.warp/supervisor.py in _CH_ENGINE). Both capabilities.yaml copies are byte-identical. docs/runbook.md (1.5 to 1.6) documents the in-session default, the opt-in external supervisor (off by default, how to enable/inspect/remove), and the no-detached-process boundary. findings.text: Non-blocking. A hypothetical raw subprocess.Popen placed directly inside install() (bypassing both the injected runner and the launch_session seam) would evade the current teeth: the launch spy patches SUP.launch_session, and the fake systemctl only observes calls routed through the runner, so neither would observe a Popen written straight into install. The shipped code is clean (no such Popen exists; the module imports no subprocess at module top and only RealSystemctl.run touches subprocess, for systemctl only), so this is recorded as a note, not a defect. A future guard could add source-inspection teeth asserting supervisor.py never references subprocess/os.fork/os.system outside RealSystemctl.run.

summary: WARP-0907 (the fleet supervisor, W7 of PLAN-0009) passes with notes at 70a9ecb, zero blocking findings. In-session resume is the wired default of warp fleet (AC1, proven by driving cmd_fleet with no waiter over a fake clock: it builds the InSessionWaiter, waits to the governor resume epoch, re-checks, and spawns nothing). The external supervisor is opt-in and off by default (AC2): nothing is scheduled or created until the user explicitly runs warp supervisor install. It is the right architecture, visible and removable (AC3): a standard systemd user timer plus oneshot service with OnCalendar from the governor resume time, enabled through an injected runner, idempotent and confined, with clean idempotent status/uninstall, all tested over a temp XDG dir and a fake systemctl so the real user systemd is never touched. The session launch is a fail-loud reference seam (AC4): install runs only systemctl subcommands and never launches a session, launch_session fails loud unwired and delegates when wired, a fabricate-a-schedule install is refused, and a spy proves install never launches a session. The module ships in the engine and all seven packs byte-identical with three honest, non-repo-only capability entries and runbook V.8 documentation (AC5). The full gate is GREEN (AC6): 1374/0 at HEAD 53461aa which carries the WARP-0907 code unchanged, 1368/0 at the isolated 70a9ecb build, template-sync and pack drift and cross-pack conformance clean, no protected path edited, index regenerated, RULE #1 clean, warp name unchanged. The safety boundary (feedback_no_rogue_processes) holds by construction: no subprocess at module top, the only subprocess use is a lazy systemctl call inside RealSystemctl, and no session spawn exists anywhere. One non-blocking note: a hypothetical raw Popen written directly into install would bypass the spy and the fake runner, but no such code exists and the shipped module is clean. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
